unresolved.reason: Exact public archaeological coordinates for Bellows O18 and Faʻahia remain unverified. Sear publishes a lake coordinate, not an ancient settlement. Broad schematic regional anchors now make the evidence viewable without substituting exact site points.
Ioannidis 2021 extended model tables and numerical confidence intervals were not independently audited. Point estimates remain in qualified claim text; no padded timeline ranges are invented.
Marquesan and Society hypotheses remain alternatives. Neither genomic network sampling nor chronological compatibility identifies an exclusive first Hawaiian homeland.
Biomarkers, archaeological basal layers, site-establishment posteriors and regional colonization models target different events and should not be silently collapsed.
Preserve full model definitions and calibration assumptions if recomputing; 67% and 95% HPDs cannot be exchanged or treated as occupation cores.
No original experimental-voyage report was supplied or independently audited here. Capability experiments can test viability but do not directly date prehistoric arrivals.
Tice item, Brown review venue, Jacobeit exact identity, alleged Emory2016 edition and Glick electronic/original edition date remain unresolved; no prehistoric claims rely on them.

Broad export assertions about forest clearance, rats, flightless bird extinction and agricultural infrastructure require dedicated source-specific dates and causal studies. No automatic all-island contemporaneity inferred.

Austronesian and Polynesian language relationships must be modeled separately from genetic ancestry, archaeological traditions and named peoples. Ioannidis background citations alone do not date a single Taiwan-to-Hawaiʻi migration.

corrections.correction: Ioannidis 2021 did not sample Hawaiʻi. It cannot directly trace the first Hawaiian colonists or date their arrival.
Athens2014 940–1130 CE (95% HPD) and 1000–1100 CE (67% HPD), Dye2011 variants, and Wilmshurst2011 1219–1266 CE differ. Preserve source-specific models and methodological debate.
Online December2010, issue February2011. Regional phase estimates are not precise dates for all islands, and Mulrooney2011 challenges selection/statistics; Wilmshurst2011 reply defends them.

Atiu is in the Southern Cook Islands. Pig/human biomarkers are indirect local indicators rather than direct Hawaiian arrival evidence. Erratum adds Emma Pearson and funding acknowledgment without changing dates.
Environmental stress is a proposed contributory explanation, not established motive for every voyage or proof of an actual modeled route.
About1050–1160 CE concerns the investigated lowest cultural layer and 12 short-lived determinations, not every Society Island or a known Hawaiian departure event.
Allen separates secure, probable and less-secure chronology evidence and retains homeland uncertainty; do not declare Marquesan origin proven.
The inspected abstract supports distinct settlement-process models, not Hawaiian settlement5000years ago.
These are book reviews; Petersen2019 is not the author of Kirch’s archaeological history, and neither review is a new primary dating program.
Travel writing, German implement inventory and an education perspective do not provide the prehistoric archaeology/experimental methods assigned to them by the export.
A 1959 Origin of the Hawaiians is bibliographically documented; the export’s2016 attribution is unresolved.
Related language families, modeled ancestry and archaeological traditions are distinct evidence. No one-to-one language–gene–people equivalence adopted.

corrections.target: Hudjashov used as original phonological evidence
corrections.correction: Hudjashov 2018 is a genomic study. Wilson 2012 supplies the primary abstract's 73 lexical/grammatical innovation claim; the input's over-200 phonological count is not adopted.
mtDNA coalescence, present-day admixture dates, rat genealogy, archaeological sample ages and inferred language splits are distinct quantities; none is silently substituted for another.
Soares explicitly questions the simple maternal-Taiwan component of a prior Slow Boat account. The inputs incorrectly collapse differing maternal models into one agreement.
3090–2258 cal BP is a modeled start boundary, not a full closed pottery occupation; possible 3903–3420 cal BP association is tentative.
Shared ancestry does not prove one route or direction. Ioannidis 2021 did not sample Hawaiʻi; the Hawaiʻi review's sampling-limit claim remains canonical.
The input's 'reverse west-to-east' phrase is geographically inconsistent. Actual source assignments and independent population histories are retained without a generic directional arrow.
Kayser 2006 percentages refer to mtDNA/Y marker classifications in studied samples, not whole-genome fractions or resident-population counts.
Cochrane 2005 is Archaeology International, not Artificial Intelligence. It emphasizes limited early mobility evidence rather than mapping all highland trails.

corrections.target: Modern Fiji identity and origin narratives
corrections.correction: Cocom's contemporary mixed-identity interviews and Jones's Biblical genealogical narratives do not establish prehistoric highland tribal genetic origins.

Vanuatu genomic transformations are not automatically Fiji highland ancestry estimates. Feldman 2026 supports distinct Fiji dispersals and a local kin/status association, not one ancestry profile for every highland community.
Ra relocation evidence includes historical/community testimony. The proposed AD 1300 climate mechanism is interpretive and does not prove universal mass flight into fortified highlands.
